product.title: Reply
product.body:
Reply spawned from Kasper Pyndt Rasmussen’s grad-work at The Royal Academy in Copenhagen (2016). The project concerned itself with tone of voice in writing by creating three distinct font styles in one weight, yet with similar vertical metrics for seamless juxtaposition; A “friendly” style, an “unfriendly” style and a “neutral” style (whatever that means) intended as an alternative to emojis in contexts like instant messaging, or to assign meaning on a micro-typographical level.

Reply was later adapted from that so-called neutral style, and over the years, little chunks of personality were carefully parsed into it making it, well, a little less neutral. The Reply of 2026 is a typeface that intends to thread the needle on the elusive expression: plain without being boring—like Beatrice Ward’s Crystal Goblet, but with a couple of chips on the rim.

Reply is a response to typography at every scale. A reply to emails, invoices, footnotes, captions and forms. A reply to the brief, “Draw Arial from memory.” And a reply that can inhabit almost any meaning and medium. Hopefully this reply can be of use to you.

product.seo_description: AT Reply is a multifunctional neo-grotesk font family. Neutral, but not boring, it adds just enough personality to make typography friendlier at every scale. It may be seen as a warmer alternative to Helvetica, Arial and other Swiss modernist fonts

brand.title: Approximate Type
brand.body:
Approximate Type, established in 2021, serves as a distribution platform and catalogue of retail typefaces created by Kasper Pyndt Rasmussen. The typefaces come from disparate starting points, but all share a healthy skepticism (but certainly not disregard) for conventions. While glancing at history, every typeface is an attempt at discovering a new formal sensibility or internal logic. They are amalgams of ambiguous personal preferences and specific visual references, and they are ever-growing and dynamic, continually modified, optimised and expanded.
